description: De la Unison para el mundo.
summary:
LuNav is an interactive lunar south-pole exploration and mission-planning platform. We developed a web application that lets users explore candidate sites in 3D, inspect terrain and horizon profiles, and simulate sunlight and Earth visibility over time. Its planning tools estimate site feasibility, flag potential shadowing and communication challenges, compare schedule delays, and suggest alternative locations. Users can also assess custom coordinates. To make lunar science accessible to more people, LuNav includes an educational Academy with interactive rover, landing, physics, and moon-base activities.

The project addresses the challenge of understanding how the Moon’s rugged polar terrain and lighting conditions could affect exploration and communications. By combining visualization, conceptual planning, and hands-on learning, LuNav supports early-stage exploration and public engagement. Its calculations are estimates for educational and exploratory use, not validated operational mission guidance.
details:
In the mission-planning workspace, users can view lunar locations in 3D, inspect 360-degree horizon profiles and a lunar polar map, and explore modeled sunlight and Earth visibility over time. The planner assesses conceptual mission feasibility, highlights potential hazards such as prolonged darkness or communication interruptions, compares schedule delays, and suggests alternative sites or routes. Users can also enter custom coordinates and elevation for an assessment. These capabilities are implemented in the explorer, planner, and simulation services.

LuNav also includes an educational Academy with interactive activities such as rover driving, lunar landing, power-grid planning, physics experiments, and moon-base building. Quizzes, field-training activities, progress levels, and achievements make lunar science and exploration concepts more engaging for learners. Academy progress is saved in the browser.

The project’s main benefits are that it brings lunar site exploration, conceptual mission planning, and space education together in one interactive experience. It is designed to help people understand how terrain, sunlight, and line-of-sight communication can affect operations near the lunar south pole, while making those topics accessible to a broader audience. Its intended impact is educational and exploratory: it can support learning and early-stage discussion of lunar missions, but it should not be treated as an operational navigation or safety-critical planning system.

The application was developed with JavaScript and React, using Vite for the frontend, Three.js/WebGL for 3D visualization, and CSS for the interface. A lightweight Node.js HTTP server provides local JSON data for candidate sites and horizon profiles. The project also includes a global lunar image texture used in its visualizations. No specialized hardware is specified; the software is intended to run in a modern web browser on a computer.

LuNav’s creative approach is to combine a cinematic lunar interface and interactive 3D exploration with analytical planning tools and arcade-style learning. The project’s features reflect considerations such as lunar terrain, location and elevation, solar illumination, Earth visibility for communications, shadowed regions, schedule changes, and different audiences, from mission explorers to students.
